summary.headline: KNR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue INR696 crore with 24.3% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance cut to ~INR2,000 crore+ revenue and 10-11% margins.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR696 crore with EBITDA of INR169 crore (24.3% margin) and net profit of INR106 crore; FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,698 crore, EBITDA INR711 crore (26.4%) and net profit INR437 crore. Standalone Q4 revenue was INR535 crore at a 5.3% EBITDA margin. Management said FY27 revenue is hard to call, pointed to around INR2,000 crore plus, and guided EBITDA margins to roughly 10-11% as lower-margin HAM and EPC work replaces high-margin irrigation. Order book stood at INR8,672 crore before two new HAM awards and INR11,903 crore after them, and FY27 order inflow target is INR8,000-10,000 crore. Telangana irrigation receivables of about INR670 crore (Kaleshwaram Package 4) remain stuck, with management expecting collection next quarter.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone EBITDA FY26 / net profit FY26

segments.name: HAM (captive/BOT)
segments.commentary: HAM contributed about 42% of Q4 revenue; the Mahabubnagar–Gudebellur project is targeted at 11-12% EBITDA and the Chennai ECR project was described as comfortable. Earlier HAM margins were about 15-16%.

segments.name: Road EPC and back-to-back EPC
segments.commentary: Road EPC was about 33% of Q4 revenue and back-to-back EPC about 17%. Mining order book is about INR3,500-3,552 crore and expected to contribute INR300-350 crore in FY28.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: Irrigation was about 8% of Q4 revenue and about INR340 crore in FY26 (17% of irrigation work done). FY27 irrigation execution is limited to Package 3 at INR200-250 crore if land acquisition is resolved; unbilled irrigation is about INR800 crore.

segments.name: Pipeline
segments.commentary: Pipeline execution was about INR270 crore in FY26 (13-14% of pipeline work); FY27 target is INR350-400 crore. Pipeline order book is about 7% of total order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: management said it is difficult to guide, but expects at least around INR2,000 crore, with FY28 revenue of around INR3,000 crore plus.
EBITDA margin guided at about 10-11% for FY27 onwards, as the order book mix shifts away from irrigation (18-20% margins historically) toward HAM and EPC.
FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000-10,000 crore across NHAI, irrigation, mining and state government work.

Two new HAM projects (Chennai ECR, INR2,163 crore bid cost; Mahabubnagar–Gudebellur, INR1,734 crore) expected to contribute about INR1,000-1,200 crore revenue in FY28 combined; financial closure of ECR expected in June 2026 and appointed date within about 2 months.
FY27 capex target of INR200-250 crore, mainly for the mining project and ECR Chennai, which may be funded by internal accruals and higher purchase loans.

Telangana irrigation receivables (about INR1,400-1,450 crore including unbilled) expected to be collected in the next quarter; mining project expected to start around Q4 FY27 after Gram Sabha, roughly 7-8 months away.
capex_capacity: Mining project (Banhardih, approx. 850 hectares): forest F1 clearance received; Gram Sabha pending, with management expecting start in about 7-8 months. Mining order is about INR3,552 crore, with capex of about INR350 crore on the parent balance sheet.
HAM equity: INR734.24 crore invested out of INR952.17 crore revised requirement as of March 31, 2026; additional INR217.93 crore in FY27 and INR47.93 crore in FY28 (per call, figures as stated).
Total capex in FY26 was about INR4 crore, per management; Q4 capex was negligible.

Monetisation: KNR Palani Infra SPV sold to Indus Infra Trust; consideration INR205.05 crore against INR64.40 crore invested and INR90 crore cash upstreamed. Closures expected June 2026 (one project) and September 2026 (two projects).
Mysore–Kushalnagara Packages IV and V are at 15.5% and 12.2% physical progress, with delays from land and service road disputes; provisional completion targeted on time but final completion may slip.
demand_pricing: Industry: NHAI awarded about 3,100 km in FY26, down about 22% YoY and below the 7,500 km target; NHAI constructed about 5,300 km. MoRTH expected to construct 9,000-9,500 km in FY27.
Order book: INR8,672 crore at March 31, 2026 (INR11,903 crore including new HAM); 61% third-party, 39% captive HAM; third-party split 59% state government, 1% central government, 1% private.
Order book mix: roads 49%, mining 30%, irrigation 14%, pipeline 7%. Execution period 3-3.5 years excluding mining.
Unbilled revenue: about INR800 crore irrigation and about INR500 crore roads.

Pipeline: about INR4,000 crore identified (GHMC flyovers, mining, Chennai ORR); bids submitted for mining (about INR3,600 crore) and Chennai ORR (about INR850 crore). Railway bids of about INR700-800 crore submitted (Lumding–Shimoga about INR800 crore).
Competition: management said new orders are being won at tight pricing; the market is at low levels after two years of low NHAI awards.
Working capital: debtor days reduced versus March 2025, excluding the Telangana irrigation dues; Kaleshwaram Package 4 debtors of about INR670 crore are stuck.

qa_highlights.question: Telangana irrigation dues: timeline for recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said KNR and Megha Engineering met the Finance Minister and expect settlement within 1-2 months, likely in the next quarter rather than the current one. Package 4 debtors of about INR670 crore have not moved.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 margin and FY28 revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said turnover may rise but bottom line will be lower, with EBITDA around 10-11%. Management also said FY28 revenue could be around INR3,000 crore plus, with Mahabubnagar HAM at about 11-13% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Mining revenue timing and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining turnover is expected at INR300-350 crore in FY28, peaking near INR1,000 crore in year five. Capex will sit on the parent balance sheet, funded through accruals, monetisation and higher purchase loans.

qa_highlights.question: Irrigation and pipeline execution in FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 irrigation execution was about INR340 crore and pipeline about INR270 crore. FY27 pipeline is targeted at INR350-400 crore, and irrigation at INR200-250 crore from Package 3 if land is cleared.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre and solar plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussion on a Hyderabad data centre with partners (MoU circulated), and is exploring utility-scale solar above 500 MW, with the land bank used for quarries and solar.

qa_highlights.question: Major delays in current projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Mysore–Kushalnagara projects were stalled by land and service-road disputes; police protection was received about two weeks before the call, and work is now in full swing. Final completion may slip beyond the scheduled date.

risks_watch: Telangana irrigation receivables of about INR670 crore (Package 4) and total Telangana dues of INR1,400-1,450 crore remain uncollected; management's timelines have slipped before.
Margin compression to 10-11% EBITDA as irrigation (historically 18-20%) falls out of the mix; FY26 EBITDA margin was 26.4% consolidated, versus 24.3% in Q4.
Order inflow of INR8,000-10,000 crore versus INR8,672 crore book and a weak NHAI award pace; FY27 revenue guidance is effectively undefined.
Mining project start depends on Gram Sabha clearance at Banhardih, with rehabilitation questions outstanding; timeline is 7-8 months.
Working capital rose on debtor stretch; net debt to equity rose to 0.49x from 0.41x.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management repeatedly declined to give firm FY27 revenue and margin guidance, citing a tight-pricing market and uncertain award timing. Confidence is higher on order pipeline and recovery of Telangana dues, which management repeatedly described as likely within one to two quarters.
